quotes.text: (Private preview) [Stripe Terminal](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal.md) supports using Klarna in-store with [additional payment methods](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/payments/additional-payment-methods.md?payment-method=klarna).
If a Klarna payment uses the `setup_future_usage` parameter, it’s considered a recurring payment, which limits the available payment options.
Germany, Sweden, and the United States are the only countries that support Pay Later for subscription and on-demand payments.

old_evidence.text: When you set the [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object.md#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) parameter, a Klarna payment isn’t considered a one-time payment.
- If the partial refund is less than the remaining balance of the order, Klarna deducts the amount from the outstanding balance and spreads refunds evenly across the remaining payments.

findings: Semantic raw delta: November reorganizes old global payment-option table into region/country toggles, per-country tables and retained all-country table (new raw lines 135-160, 251-614, 614-763; old raw lines 121-270; diff lines 3-699). This is substantially presentational but also contains concrete changed availability/range claims, not a pure navigation change.

November adds Italy one-time Financing at 35-3,000 EUR to both Italy and all-country tables; old financing table omits Italy (new raw lines 452-468, 735-753; old raw lines 242-258; diff lines 373-389, 648-687). Klarna approval remains subject to creditworthiness in the row, and listing does not prove a particular buyer's eligibility.

Pay in 3 EUR ceiling for France, Ireland, Italy and Spain rises in the captured tables from 1,500 to 3,000 (new raw lines 399-401, 448-450, 465-467, 367-369, 721-725; old raw lines 228-241; diff lines 627-631). Geographic/cart ranges are determined by Klarna and can change (new raw lines 135-143; old raw lines 121-123).

November adds a Klarna in-store Stripe Terminal private-preview mention and request-access form (new raw lines 119-133; old raw lines 107-119; diff lines 32-54). It is neither generally available Terminal support nor evidence that access was requested or granted.

Existing-summary baseline accuracy: source line 25 says recurring options are 'Not available with setup_future_usage', but old raw line 260 and new raw line 143 say this parameter classifies the payment as recurring and limits visible plans; they do not categorically prohibit it. Source line 23's Financing country list omits November Italy; source line 29's EEA-focused cross-border wording omits UK and Switzerland business rows (old raw lines 276-288; new raw lines 783-794).

Source line 33 says partial refunds spread evenly across remaining installments without the condition: both captures say when refund is less than remaining balance it is deducted and spread, while a greater refund returns the excess (old raw lines 290-297; new raw lines 796-803). Source line 17's 'Broadest BNPL on Stripe' is an unsupported comparison to other methods in these captures (old raw lines 14-100; new raw lines 15-101).

Source frontmatter lines 1-9 lacks canonical_url and raw_files/Raw Sources lines 6-7, 39-41 route only May raw; retain May provenance while adding November raw. Root wiki/index.md line 7 -> wiki/stripe-index.md lines 332 and 686; wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md lines 262-268 routes source, whereas wiki/concepts/stripe-klarna.md lines 44-46 only routes subscription source. The BNPL concept line 20 says Klarna 22 countries while both overview captures list 23 customer countries (old raw lines 16-18; new raw lines 17-19).
substantive_changes: Italy Financing appears as a one-time option at 35-3,000 EUR in November country and all-country tables, absent from May Financing list (new raw lines 452-468, 735-753; old raw lines 242-258).
November Pay in 3 range for France, Ireland, Italy and Spain is 1-3,000 EUR versus May 1-1,500 EUR (new raw lines 721-725; old raw lines 228-241).
November documents Klarna on Stripe Terminal only as private preview with an access-request route (new raw lines 119-133; old raw lines 107-119).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain May's 2026-05-06 country/currency/range tables as historical, including 23 customer countries, 32 business countries, 13 presentment currencies, no Italy Financing and 1,500 EUR Pay in 3 ceiling for FR/IE/IT/ES (old raw lines 14-100, 121-258; source lines 17-23). Do not recast all old rows as current November rows.

Both captures say Klarna redirects the customer to choose a plan and returns them to the merchant; merchant receives the order amount minus fees when payment is accepted, while standard payout timing applies and Klarna bears consumer repayment loss (old raw lines 8-13, 36-38; new raw lines 9-13, 37-39). Return and acceptance do not prove immediate funds availability, settlement, buyer approval or dispute immunity.

Keep setup_future_usage qualification: old raw line 260 says it makes payment not one-time and can hide otherwise eligible plans in Payment Method Messaging Element and Payment Element; new raw line 143 frames it as recurring classification/limited options across hosted, embedded and Elements. Neither says recurring payments generally unavailable.

Keep May explicit cross-border routes: EEA, UK and Switzerland businesses may present to EEA/UK/Swiss buyers in the customer local currency; other countries are domestic with business local currency (old raw lines 272-288; new raw lines 779-794). Keep 180-day refund window and conditional partial-refund allocation (old raw lines 290-297; new raw lines 796-803).

Keep Connect and buyer-country conditions: all charge types, connected-account Dashboard/capability distinction, and shipping-address then geocoded-IP filtering (old raw lines 299-318; new raw lines 805-824). The May guide's B2B restriction is reiterated in November (old raw lines 107-119; new raw lines 107-121).

Do not infer Finland Pay in 3 availability from the removed old footnote: May footnote 268 mentions Finland although its option country list omits it (old raw lines 207-241); November footnote 761 omits Finland and Finland country table lists Pay in full, Pay later and Financing only (new raw lines 371-384).
conflicts: Internal November tension: country Pay Later rows for Austria, Belgium, Switzerland, Czechia, Denmark, Spain, Finland, France, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania and UK list subscription use cases (new raw lines 251-282, 284-313, 337-398, 403-415, 452-495, 501-545), yet the all-country footnote and limitations say only Germany, Sweden and US support Pay Later for subscriptions and on-demand (new raw lines 759, 775). The old footnote also says only DE/SE/US (old raw line 266). Do not resolve as expanded subscription eligibility.

Old Finland Pay in 3/4 one-time-only footnote conflicts with absence of Finland from the old Pay in 3/4 country row; November omits Finland from both country table and footnote (old raw lines 207-241, 268; new raw lines 371-384, 696-717, 761). Omission does not establish Finland installments.

Current source line 25's blanket setup_future_usage unavailability contradicts both captures' recurring classification/limited display (old raw line 260; new raw line 143). Source line 33's unconditional even spreading conflicts with both refund branches (old raw lines 292-295; new raw lines 798-801).
unresolved_questions: Which November Pay Later country table use cases are authoritative for subscription eligibility given the repeated only-DE/SE/US footnote (new raw lines 261-264, 280-282, 759, 775)? Resolve before advising country-specific subscription launch.

Does an actual merchant or customer qualify for Italy Financing, the higher Pay in 3 ceilings, or Klarna Terminal preview? The captured country ranges and preview invitation do not verify account eligibility or approval (new raw lines 119-133, 135-143, 452-468, 721-753).

source_assessments.reason: The November capture includes substantive country/range and private-preview additions, while the mapped source has baseline factual overstatements and missing provenance. A dated source correction with reciprocal warnings is needed.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna, Klarna offers a customer-initiated redirect where the buyer sees plan options based on location, currency, amount and use case; on accepted payment the merchant receives the order amount minus fees in Stripe, while Klarna handles customer repayment and bears that loss, with standard payout timing still applying (new raw lines 7-55; old raw lines 4-54). The November capture keeps 23 customer and 32 business countries, 13 currencies, four plan families, cross-border EEA/UK/Swiss versus domestic rules, refund and Connect distinctions (new raw lines 17-101, 135-143, 779-824; old raw lines 16-100, 121-123, 272-318). It adds Italy one-time Financing at 35-3,000 EUR, raises FR/IE/IT/ES Pay in 3 ceiling to 3,000 EUR, and describes Terminal as private preview (new raw lines 119-133, 452-468, 721-753; old raw lines 228-258). The mapped source-stripe-klarna.md summarizes the May guide but wrongly says setup_future_usage is unavailable and omits new options and UK/Swiss business cross-border rows (current source lines 17-33). B2B is excluded, available plans depend on eligibility, and redirect/acceptance does not establish immediate payout settlement.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna, the November region/country toggles and repeated all-country table are largely presentation, while Italy Financing 35-3,000 EUR, FR/IE/IT/ES Pay in 3 ceiling 1,500 to 3,000 EUR, and Terminal private preview are documented deltas (new raw lines 119-160, 452-468, 721-753; old raw lines 107-123, 228-258). source-stripe-klarna.md must retain May provenance and dated limits, add November raw and canonical_url, correct its blanket setup_future_usage prohibition, preserve UK/Swiss business cross-border rows, and condition partial-refund allocation on remaining balance (current source lines 1-9, 23-33, 39-41; old raw lines 260, 276-295; new raw lines 143, 783-801). The November Pay Later country tables list subscriptions beyond DE/SE/US but its footnote and limitations still say only those three countries; preserve that conflict instead of asserting expansion (new raw lines 251-282, 759, 775; old raw line 266). Finland's removed Pay in 3 footnote does not add a Finland option, since the new Finland table lacks it (old raw lines 207-241, 268; new raw lines 371-384, 761). Display, credit approval, merchant access, payment acceptance and payout availability remain distinct.
